name: Gleirschklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The Gleirschklamm gorge near Scharnitz in the Karwendel Nature Park: primeval gorge trail along the roaring Gleirschbach stream with wooden walkways and a history of timber rafting.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wild and romantic Gleirschklamm gorge is located in the heart of the Karwendel Nature Park, Austria's largest nature park, in the municipality of Scharnitz in the Seefeld region at an altitude of around 1,000 meters above sea level. Carved between the rugged rock peaks of the Erlspitz group and the Gleirsch-Halltal chain, the gorge is one of the most unspoiled natural wonders of North Tyrol. Along the roaring Gleirschbach stream, a spectacular, narrow rock path leads through a dramatic gorge landscape characterized by thundering cascades, deep blue pools, and towering limestone walls. The geological roots of the Gleirschklamm gorge date back over 230 million years to the Mesozoic era (Triassic), when the steep gorge walls of massive Wetterstein limestone were formed in a tropical shallow sea.

Route & Requirements

Folded by tectonic shifts and cut by the permanent deep erosion of the meltwater stream, the mountain stream still exposes fossil remains of prehistoric marine organisms today. In addition to its geology, the gorge is closely intertwined with Tyrol's economic history: for centuries, the Gleirschtal valley was an important center for Karwendel timber rafting. Huge quantities of felled round timber were rafted down the narrow rock gorge and further via the Isar river during the spring snowmelt to supply the salt pans of the Saline Hall in Tirol with firewood.

Visit & Arrival

The Gleirschklamm gorge is freely accessible during the snow-free months from mid-May to the end of October. During the winter months from November to May, the gorge is officially closed for safety reasons due to avalanche and rockfall danger. Access to the gorge is completely free of charge. Arrival by public transport is by S-Bahn Tirol (line S6) or REX of the Karwendelbahn directly to Scharnitz train station; from there, it's about a 45-minute walk via the Nature Park Info Center and the Scharnitzer Alm to the gorge entrance.

Tips

Due to the narrow rock path, wet wooden planks, and uneven steps, the Gleirschklamm gorge is absolutely not barrier-free and unsuitable for strollers. Sure-footed hiking boots with sturdy profiled soles and a head for heights are essential. The path is not recommended for toddlers. The Gleirschklamm circular hike, with a walking time of approx. 3.5 hours, is very rewarding. After passing through the gorge, you continue on the forest road to the idyllic Möslalm (1,262 m) for a Tyrolean Brettljause (cold platter) and return to Scharnitz via the scenic Nederweg through shady mountain forest. This tour offers a perfect combination of nature experience and alpine refreshment and provides unforgettable impressions for your entire holiday in Tyrol.
preis: Free access (parking at In der Länd subject to charge)
oeffnungszeiten: Mid-May to end of October open during the day (closed in winter)
